intro.text: The helmswoman of the Crow's Song, who trades a pair of gold earrings won at cards to Fort for a pocket watch.
The helmswoman of the Crow's Song, who searches every port for her father so that she can pay off his debts.
Helmswoman of the Two Cups, now sailing with the father she spent years looking for.

items.text: Salay grew up on the Islands of Lobu in the Sapphire Sea. When her father fell into debt, she swore to clear it by working as a helmswoman, but the king's collectors took him for forced labour first. He was moved from one debtors' prison to another and pressed onto royal ships in between, and she kept sailing in hope of tracking him down.

Salay had gone along with the crew's turn to piracy because she would not give up sailing, and she looked for her father at each port they visited. After Crow kicked Tress, Salay checked her for injuries and let her take the wheel, explaining that at the helm her authority was absolute, even over the captain.

When Crow ordered sabres out to board a captured ship, Salay claimed the helmswoman's right to deal with its crew and reminded Crow that they had turned pirate for freedom, not for killing. Crow gave way.

Sure that Tress was a King's Mask, one of the king's secret agents, Salay brought her to a hidden meeting with Fort and Ann about Crow. There they hit on persuading Crow to sail the emptier Crimson Sea instead of raiding more ships.

On the Crimson Sea she handled the ship so well through walls of crimson spikes that even Crow obeyed her orders, but a crewman, Pakson, was killed. Blaming herself, Salay told Tress of her frustrated search for her father, and Tress in turn told her about the dragon and her own goal of reaching the Sorceress.

Salay joined the officers in planning a mutiny, but Crow had them watched. Laggart shot Salay in the thigh, and in the fight that followed she reached for a gun and was put down. Only then did she understand that Tress was no King's Mask.

Ulaam's salve sped the healing of her leg, and Tress came back from the dragon with a note telling Salay where her father was. Salay refused to let Tress sail on without her, saying that part of the helm's job was to stop a captain making bad decisions.
Salay tried to stop Tress rowing into the Midnight Sea alone, suggesting safer ways to test her plan and insisting the crew wanted to help, but Tress would not be moved.

When Tress did not come back, the crew went after her. Salay guided the ship past the rocks around the Sorceress's island and asked Hoid why Tress believed he could save her, but his curse kept him from answering.

With Fort and Ann she got Hoid into the tower in time to save Tress and Charlie and send the Sorceress away. The crew then swapped the Crow's Song for a larger ship, the Two Cups, found Salay's father and took him on as her apprentice at the helm, and grew rich trading across the Crimson and Midnight Seas.

appearance.text: Short and dark-skinned, with tight black curls and delicate features. At the helm she wears a coat and stiff trousers.

personality.text: Quick-tempered but fiercely loyal, she takes every loss among the crew personally. Ann thinks she is a poor judge of people, yet she has the nerve to defy Crow and to sail the deadliest seas.

items.text: An expert at the helm, she charts the distance sailed, steers clear of storms where she can, and by custom deals with the captains of captured ships. She brought the Crow's Song through sea battles, crimson storms and the rocks around the Sorceress's island.
